arxiv-1509-04265.title: Double Relief with progressive weighting function
arxiv-1509-04265.creator: Gabriel Prat Masramon, Lluís A. Belanche Muñoz
arxiv-1509-04265.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Gabriel Prat Masramon, Lluís A. Belanche Muñoz. Feature weighting algorithms try to solve a problem of great importance nowadays in machine learning: The search of a relevance measure for the features of a given domain. This relevance is primarily used for feature selection as feature weighting can be seen as a generalization of it, but it is also useful to better understand a problem’s domain or to guide an inductor in its learning process.

arxiv-2102-08296.title: Geodesic random walks, diffusion processes and Brownian motion on Finsler manifolds.
arxiv-2102-08296.creator: Tianyu Ma, Vladimir S. Matveev, Ilya Pavlyukevich
arxiv-2102-08296.description: Abstract We show that geodesic random walks on a complete Finsler manifold of bounded geometry converge to a diffusion process which is, up to a drift, the Brownian motion corresponding to a Riemannian metric. MSC 2000: 53B40, 53C60, 82B41, 82C41 Key words: Geodesic random walks, weak convergence, Finsler manifold, diffusion process, Riemannian Brownian motion, averaged metric, bounded geometry. 1 Introduction.

arxiv-2103-14458.title: A micropolar continuum model of diffusion creep
arxiv-2103-14458.creator: John F. Rudge, John F. Rudge
arxiv-2103-14458.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by John F. Rudge, John F. Rudge. Solid polycrystalline materials undergoing diffusion creep are usually described by Cauchy continuum models with a Newtonian viscous rheology dependent on the grain size. Such a continuum lacks the rotational degrees of freedom needed to describe grain rotation. Here we provide a more general continuum description of diffusion creep that includes grain rotation, and identifies the deformation of the material with that of a micropolar (Cosserat) fluid.

arxiv-2109-03135.title: Tensor Monopoles in Superconducting Systems
arxiv-2109-03135.creator: Hannes Weisbrich, Markus Bestler, Wolfgang Belzig
arxiv-2109-03135.description: Abstract Topology in general but also topological objects such as monopoles are a central concept in physics. They are prime examples for the intriguing physics of gauge theories and topological states of matter. Vector monopoles are already frequently discussed such as the well-established Dirac monopole in three dimensions. Less known are tensor monopoles giving rise to tensor gauge fields.

arxiv-2204-03292.title: Robust Controllers for a Flexible Satellite Model Thanks: The research was supported by the Academy of Finland grants 298182, 310489 and 349002. J.-P. Humaloja is funded by grants from the Jenny and Antti Wihuri Foundation and the Vilho, Yrjö and Kalle Väisälä Foundation
arxiv-2204-03292.creator: Thavamani Govindaraj, Jukka-Pekka Humaloja, Lassi Paunonen
arxiv-2204-03292.description: Abstract . We consider a PDE-ODE model of a flexible satellite that is composed of two identical flexible solar panels and a center rigid body. We prove that the satellite model is exponentially stable in the sense that the energy of the solutions decays to zero exponentially.

arxiv-2209-05332.title: Foundations of the Wald Space for Phylogenetic Trees
arxiv-2209-05332.creator: Jonas Lueg, Maryam K. Garba, Tom M. W. Nye, Stephan F. Huckemann
arxiv-2209-05332.description: Abstract . Evolutionary relationships between species are represented by phylogenetic trees, but these relationships are subject to uncertainty due to the random nature of evolution. A geometry for the space of phylogenetic trees is necessary in order to properly quantify this uncertainty during the statistical analysis of collections of possible evolutionary trees inferred from biological data.

arxiv-2504-11775.title: Discrimination-Free Insurance Pricing with Privatized Sensitive Attributes
arxiv-2504-11775.creator: Tianhe Zhang, Suhan Liu, Peng Shi
arxiv-2504-11775.description: Abstract Fairness has become an important concern in insurance pricing as insurers increasingly rely on machine learning models to predict expected losses. At the same time, regulatory and privacy constraints often restrict insurers’ ability to access or use sensitive attributes such as gender or race.

arxiv-2511-18734.title: Yo’City: Personalized and Boundless 3D Realistic City Scene Generation via Self-Critic Expansion
arxiv-2511-18734.creator: Keyang Lu, Sifan Zhou, Hongbin Xu, Gang Xu, Zhifei Yang, Yikai Wang, Zhen Xiao, Jieyi Long, Ming Li
arxiv-2511-18734.description: Abstract Realistic 3D city generation is fundamental to a wide range of applications, including virtual reality and digital twins. However, most existing methods rely on training a single diffusion model, which limits their ability to generate personalized and boundless city-scale scenes.

arxiv-2602-05182.title: The Single-Multi Evolution Loop for Self-Improving Model Collaboration Systems
arxiv-2602-05182.creator: Shangbin Feng, Kishan Panaganti, Yulia Tsvetkov, Wenhao Yu
arxiv-2602-05182.description: Abstract Model collaboration — systems where multiple language models (LMs) collaborate — combines the strengths of diverse models with cost in loading multiple LMs. We improve efficiency while preserving the strengths of collaboration by distilling collaborative patterns into a single model , where the model is trained on the outputs of the model collaboration system.

pmc-11349911.title: Post-spinel-type AB2O4 high-pressure phases in geochemistry and materials science
pmc-11349911.creator: Masaki Akaogi, Takayuki Ishii, Kazunari Yamaura
pmc-11349911.description: Post-spinel-type AB2O4 compounds are stable at higher pressures than spinel phases. These compounds have garnered much interest in geo- and materials science for their geochemical importance as well as potential application as high ionic conductors and materials with strongly correlated electrons. Here, large-volume high-pressure syntheses, structural features and properties of post-spinels are reviewed.

pmc-11674264.title: Effects of Language Proficiency on Selective Attention Patterns at Segmenting Boundaries in English Audio Sentences
pmc-11674264.creator: Yunhao Mei, Fei Chen, Xiaoxiang Chen
pmc-11674264.description: Background/Objectives: Normative perceptual segmentation facilitates event perception, comprehension, and memory. Given that native English listeners’ normative perceptual segmentation of English speech streams coexists with a highly selective attention pattern at segmentation boundaries, it is significant to test whether Chinese learners of English have a different attention pattern at boundaries, thereby checking whether they perform a normative segmentation.

pmc-12584579.title: Coronary Ectasia and ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction Patients: Does Atherosclerosis Influence Periprocedural Management and Long‐Term Prognosis?
pmc-12584579.creator: Victorine Fraichot, Jeanne Varlot, Florian Eggenspieler, Nassima Djaballah, Pierre Adrien Metzdorf, Edoardo Camenzind, Batric Popovic
pmc-12584579.description: BackgroundCoronary artery ectasia (CAE) influences procedural outcomes in the context of ST‐elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI); however, its relationship with atherosclerotic coronary artery disease (ACAD) remains unclear.AimsThis study aimed to compare clinical and procedural characteristics, as well as outcomes, in patients with STEMI and CAE, with or without coexisting ACAD.

pmc-12653875.creator: Sven Ljubić, Maja Matulić, Damir Đermić, Maria Chiara Feliciello, Alfredo Procino, Francesco Passaro, Đurđica Ugarković, Isidoro Feliciello, Grzegorz Wegrzyn, Naoyuki Kataoka
pmc-12653875.description: Satellite DNAs are highly abundant sequences that build functional centromeres and pericentromeric heterochromatin in many eukaryotes. Apart from this structural role, their involvement in gene expression modulation has been demonstrated, although a detailed understanding of the molecular mechanisms is still lacking.
